chunks: Have you not considered the leaders among the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to their prophet, 'Send forth to us a king, that we may fight in the way of Allah'? He said, 'Would it be if fighting were prescribed for you, that you would not fight?' They said, 'And why should we not fight in the way of Allah, since we have been driven out from our homes and our children?' But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them; and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
ai.seo_question: What happened when the Children of Israel were commanded to fight after demanding a king?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from prophetic leadership to monarchical rule, often linked to the appointment of Talut (Saul) as a test of obedience. The scholars note that the majority's reluctance to fight, despite their claims of devotion, reveals a fundamental flaw in their faith and readiness to sacrifice, contrasting with the few who remained steadfast. This narrative serves as a cautionary tale against the superficiality of religious commitment when tested by duty.
